question: Where is the MOST oil in the world?

post.premise: The country sitting on the most oil pumps almost none of it
post.bait: It is not Saudi Arabia, and it is not Russia.
keywords: which country has the most oil
most oil reserves in the world
post.sources_line: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2025; U.S. Energy Information Administration; Britannica

youtube.title: Which country has the most oil reserves in the world? Not Saudi Arabia 🛢️
youtube.description:
Saudi Arabia, Russia or the third one? One country sits on more proven oil than any other on Earth, nearly all of it in a single belt along one river, and it pumps barely any of it.
Guess before the map fills, then watch the bars, see the belt drawn, and the gap between what it holds and what it sells.
Which flag did you pick?

threads.text: Where is the most oil in the world — Saudi Arabia, Russia or Venezuela? One of them sits on more proven oil than any other country, nearly all of it in a single belt along one river, and it pumps barely one percent of the world's supply.

intent: The oil misdirect: Saudi Arabia is the name, Russia the size, but Venezuela holds the most proven oil on Earth — shown as bars, located as a drawn belt along the Orinoco, and undercut by a split between what it holds and what it pumps.

v04.text: Venezuela. More than 300 billion barrels of proven oil sit under it, more than any other country on Earth.

v05.text: Saudi Arabia is second with about 267 billion. Russia is far down the list.

v06.text: Nearly all of it lies in the Orinoco Belt, a strip of heavy, tar-like crude along a single river.

v07.text: Yet it pumps barely 1 percent of the world's oil; the richest reserve on Earth mostly stays underground.

v08.text: Richer than you thought. Follow us.

research.topic: Country with the most proven crude oil reserves: Venezuela — 303.2 billion barrels (OPEC ASB 2025, end-2024), ≈ 19 % of the world's 1,567 billion; Saudi Arabia 267.2 billion second; Iran, Canada, Iraq follow; Russia ≈ 80 billion; nearly all of Venezuela's reserves are extra-heavy crude in the Orinoco Belt; Venezuelan output ≈ 0.9–1.0 million b/d ≈ 1 % of world supply (~103 million b/d)

myths.myth: Saudi Arabia has the most oil in the world.
myths.reality: Saudi Arabia produces more, but Venezuela holds the most proven reserves — 303 billion barrels against Saudi Arabia's 267 billion (OPEC 2025).

landscape.our_gap: Oil Shorts rank producers or retell the Venezuelan collapse; nobody asks the reserves question on a map, shows the bars, draws the belt and splits what is held against what is pumped.

eia_world.notes: world petroleum and liquids production ≈ 103 million b/d in 2025 — Venezuela's ~0.9–1.0 million b/d is about 1 %

opec_prod.title: Monthly Oil Market Report — crude production by secondary sources
opec_prod.notes: Venezuela crude output ≈ 0.9–1.0 million b/d in 2025

reuters_ven.title: Venezuela oil output and exports (2025 coverage)
reuters_ven.notes: output around 0.9–1.1 million b/d against ~103 million b/d global liquids supply — roughly 1 %

britannica_orinoco.title: Orinoco Belt / Venezuela — resources
britannica_orinoco.notes: the Orinoco Belt (Faja del Orinoco), a strip north of the lower Orinoco River, holds one of the world's great accumulations of extra-heavy crude and bitumen

wiki_reserves.notes: Venezuela 303 bn, Saudi Arabia 267 bn, Iran 209 bn, Canada 163 bn, Iraq 145 bn; Russia ≈ 80 bn (8th)
